title: Indirect Identification via Sensor Data
description: GPS coordinates and timestamps could be combined to infer user's location patterns, enabling indirect identification even if direct identifiers are removed.
assumptions: Data is stored or transmitted without sufficient anonymization.
uncertainty_note: Node I.2.1 assumed for indirect identification; exact LINDDUN Pro node may vary.

title: Unauthorized Data Access
description: Sensor telemetry (e.g., heart rate, GPS) could be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties during transmission or storage.
assumptions: Data lacks encryption or access controls.

title: Data Use Beyond Consent
description: Collected data may be repurposed for secondary uses (e.g., marketing, insurance profiling) without explicit user consent.
assumptions: Privacy policy is vague or consent mechanisms are inadequate.

title: Lack of Transparency in Data Collection
description: User may be unaware of the extent of data collected (e.g., continuous GPS tracking) or how it is processed.
assumptions: Device UI/notifications do not clearly disclose data practices.

title: Data Linkability for Profiling
description: Combining heart rate, step counts, and GPS data could create detailed behavioral or health profiles linked to the user.
assumptions: Data is aggregated or analyzed across multiple sources.
uncertainty_note: Node L.1.1 assumed for profile creation; exact LINDDUN Pro node may vary.
